sentences.text: 3. This appeal has been referred to Mediation Centre, Bengaluru.
Accordingly, adjudicatory process has been conducted between the parties in the rank of appellants and respondents.
The appellants have preferred the appeal before this Court by urging various grounds.

In the meanwhile, the NC:
2023:KHC:39515-DB matter has been referred to Mediation Centre, Bengaluru for settlement of issues emerged between the parties.

4. Wherein the Memorandum of Settlement under Section 89 of CPC read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005, the 1st and 2nd appellants have attended mediation through their power of attorney holder Mr. Amit R Jain who is son of the 1st appellant and brother of the 2nd appellant.
The said power of attorney is already on record before the trial Court in commercial Arbitration Application No.188/2021 and copy of the same is produced in this appeal for the purpose of reference.
Respondent No.1 is represented by the president who had present along with their registered power of attorney holder before the Mediation Centre.
But today the president namely Chennegowda is present along with registered power of attorney holder.
The respondent No.3 is present for self as 3 and 4 and also representing Respondent No.2 as a partner and as a authorized signatory.
5. The appellants and respondents have entered into compromise out of their own free will and volition to settle their NC: 2023:KHC:39515-DB disputes and differences.

The appellants and respondents submitted that the Memorandum of Understanding dated 06.06.2018 and General Power of Attorney dated 12.06.2018 entered into between Respondent No.1 and Respondent No.2 for securing the TDR or other compensation from the BDA for the land relinquished by respondent No.1 to the extent of 2,44,200 square feet to the BDA, is still valid and subsisting.
Respondent No.1 has affixed its signature to the present compromise petition in due confirmation of the said fact.
The same is observed.

6. The terms and conditions of the compromise between Appellants and respondents reveals as :
a. The appellants shall be entitled to 50,000 sq.ft of the TDR to be given to Respondent No.2 in terms of the Memorandum of Understanding aforementioned between Respondent No.1 and Respondent No.2.
The said TDR is to be provided by the BDA to the Respondent No.1 towards the compensation for the land of Respondent No.1 acquired by the BDA.
The NC: 2023:KHC:39515-DB Respondent No.1 shall hand over the TDR to Respondent Nos.2 and 4 who shall in turn transfer the same to the appellants.

b. In the event TDR is not issued to the Respondent No.1 by the BDA and only compensation towards acquisition of land is provided in such circumstances 15% of the total compensation provided to the Respondent No.1 and the same shall be paid to appellants as per the Memorandum of Understanding between the appellants and the Respondent No.2.

c. In the alternate and in the event of the Respondent No.1 not being provided either TDR or compensation for acquisition of land, the Respondent Mrs R Chanchal vs The Coffee Board Employees on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87070800/
4 No.2 has agreed to refund a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs Only) with interest thereon at 24% to be computed from the date of payment till the date of refund in entirety.

sentences.text:
Whereas in clause 4 of the Mediation report the parties arrived into settlement as :
The appellants and Respondent No.2 represented by Respondent No.3 confirm that the present compromise shall constitute a decree and executable by the appellants as the circumstances may warrant for the Deed of Sale of TDR; or for payment of 15% of the compensation; or for refund of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 24% p.a. as agreed.
8. This is the settlement arrived between the parties stated supra and the report of Mediation Centre is submitted for consideration.
Whereas, Amit R Jain who is the power of attorney for appellant Nos.1 and 2 is present before the Court physically.
Respondent No.1 - Chennegowda is also present.
Respondent No.3 namely Sathish Chandra who also represents Respondent No.2 is present before the Court physically.

However, in the presence of said parties to the appeal proceedings report of mediation centre has been recorded and whereby the appellants and respondents arrived at settlement NC: 2023:KHC:39515-DB and settlement agreement has been entered between the parties and more so the conditions stated supra in Mediation Report have been appraised to them and they have submitted their acceptance.
Accordingly, the report submitted by the Mediation Centre, Bengaluru dated 29.09.2023 is hereby accepted.

9. Consequent upon acceptance of the Mediation report in the presence of learned counsels as well as respective parties this appeal is hereby disposed of in terms of compromise arrived between the parties.
